summary: This article explains how the spine is built and protected, and how good posture, light backpacks, safe lifting, and exercise keep a back strong.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “A Strong Back” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: the small bones that are stacked to make the spine
a flat, round part; in the spine, a soft pad between two bones
thin parts of the body that carry messages to and from the brain

challengeTerms.def: able to bend easily without breaking
the group of muscles in the stomach and back that keep the body steady
the way you hold your body when you sit or stand

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that schools should check how heavy students' backpacks are? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the spine, discs, and muscles work together.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review vertebrae, disc, and nerves, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses flexible, core, and posture to suggest a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
